q.s: Which of the following Early Harappan sites anticipates Mature Harappan buildings and pottery?
q.x: Kot Diji (like Kalibangan) shows pre-urban forms that anticipate the Mature Harappan phase, pointing to gradual, local urbanisation; the others are Neolithic/Chalcolithic sites outside the Harappan zone.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the origin of Harappan urbanisation is correct?
o: It was gradual and local, as Early Harappan sites anticipate it.
It began suddenly with no earlier settled phase.
It followed the arrival of the Vedic Aryans.
It was imported directly from Mesopotamia.
q.x: Kalibangan and Kot Diji anticipate Mature Harappan forms, though the gap from Neolithic Mehrgarh is not fully bridged.

q.s: Harappan cities were laid out on which pattern?
o: Irregular pattern along a river bank
Grid pattern with streets crossing at right angles
Radial pattern around a central temple
q.x: Harappan streets ran north-south and east-west, crossing at right angles, with house doors opening on side lanes.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Harappan town planning?
o: Division into citadel and lower town
Large temples at the centre of towns
q.x: No temples or palaces have been identified in Harappan cities.

q.s: Which animal is the most common motif on Harappan seals?
q.x: The one-horned 'unicorn' is the commonest seal motif; the humped bull is also frequent.

q.s: Which of the following animals is NOT depicted on Harappan seals?
q.x: The cow is not shown on Harappan seals, while the rhinoceros, humped bull and tiger are.

q.s: Which of the following is cited in support of the view that the Harappans were ruled by priests?
q.x: The citadels, the Great Bath and the steatite 'Priest-King' bust are cited for priestly rule, though the evidence is not conclusive.

q.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Late Harappan phase?
q.x: The Late Harappan phase was chalcolithic with regionally varied pottery; the uniformity of seals, bricks and weights and long-distance trade were lost.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mature Harappan phase?
q.x: The Harappans were a Bronze Age people; iron came much later.

q.s: Coins of which Shaka ruler were re-struck by Gautamiputra Satakarni?
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Kshaharata Nahapana and re-struck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard).

q.s: According to the Nasik Prashasti, Gautamiputra Satakarni destroyed all of the following EXCEPT the:
q.x: He is hailed as the destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.

q.s: In the Rig Veda, the Panis are described as:
q.x: The Panis were non-Aryan cattle-holders and traders condemned for their greed.

q.s: In the later Vedic period, the teacher who taught the Veda for a livelihood was called:
q.x: The Upadhyaya taught for a livelihood, while the Acharya taught the Veda without charging a fee.

q.s: Initiation into Vedic study was marked by which samskara?
q.x: Upanayana initiated Vedic study; Chudakarma was only the tonsure of the child.

q.s: The Mahavamsa, the Sri Lankan Buddhist chronicle, was written in:
q.x: The Mahavamsa of Mahanama is in Pali; the Dohakosa is in Apabhramsa and the Divyavadana in Sanskrit.

q.s: Which of the following Buddhist texts is NOT in Pali?
q.x: The Divyavadana is in Sanskrit.

q.s: The four gateways (toranas) of the Sanchi stupa were added under the:
q.x: The toranas are Satavahana additions; the Shungas gave the stone casing and railings.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Sanchi stupa is correct?
o: It is located in Uttar Pradesh.
It was first built by Kanishka.
It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.
Its four toranas were added under the Shungas.
q.x: Sanchi (Raisen, MP) was begun under Ashoka; the toranas are Satavahana work.

q.s: The atomic theory of the Ajivikas influenced which later school of philosophy?
q.x: The Vaisheshika is the atomist school of Indian philosophy, influenced by Ajivika ideas.

q.s: Who among the following was the leader of the Ajivika sect?
q.x: Makkhali Gosala led the Ajivikas; Ajita Kesakambalin was a materialist teacher.

q.s: Ramatirtham, an important Jain hill centre of Andhra, is in which district?
q.x: Ramatirtham in Vizianagaram district was a Jain (and Buddhist) hill centre.

q.s: The medical work Kalyanakaraka was written at Ramatirtham by:
q.x: Ugradityacharya, a Jain teacher, wrote the Kalyanakaraka at Ramatirtham.

q.s: In Kautilya's Saptanga theory of the state, which element comes last?
q.x: The order is Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda and Mitra.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven elements of Kautilya's Saptanga theory?
q.x: Shatru (enemy) is not one of the seven elements.

q.s: Which Ashokan edict, discovered in 1915, first proved that 'Piyadasi' was Ashoka?
q.x: The Maski minor rock edict in Raichur district names 'Ashoka', confirming the identity.

q.s: Kanaganahalli, where a stone portrait of Ashoka labelled 'Ranyo Asoko' was found, is on the banks of which river?
q.x: Kanaganahalli near Sannati (Karnataka) is on the Bhima.

q.s: Who among the following was the author of the Sanskrit drama Ratnavali?
q.x: Harshavardhana wrote Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda; Banabhatta was his court poet.

q.s: Grahavarman, husband of Harsha's sister Rajyashri, belonged to which dynasty?
q.x: Grahavarman was the Maukhari king of Kannauj.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a ruler of the Pushyabhuti dynasty?
q.x: Grahavarman was a Maukhari, Harsha's brother-in-law.

q.s: The first round of the Chalukya-Pallava conflict was fought between Pulakesin II and:
q.x: Pulakesin II fought Mahendravarman I first; Narasimhavarman I defeated him in the second round and took Vatapi.

q.s: Madhura Vijayam, which describes the conquest of the Madurai Sultanate, was written by:
q.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam.

q.s: Which Telugu Brahmin convert became the wazir of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
q.x: Malik Maqbul (Khan-i-Jahan), originally Jagannatha Pandit, became Firoz Shah's wazir.

q.s: After its capture by the Tughlaqs in 1323, Warangal was renamed:
q.x: Warangal became Sultanpur; Daulatabad was the renamed Devagiri.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq is correct?
o: Prataparudra II died in the Godavari while being taken to Delhi.
He was Governor of Punjab under Balban.
He limited any increase in land revenue to about one-tenth in a year.
q.x: He was Alauddin's governor, Warangal became Sultanpur, and Prataparudra II died in the Narmada.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, an iqta was:
o: A military rank based on horses
An assignment of revenue in lieu of salary
q.x: The iqta was a transferable revenue assignment, not ownership; muqtis were rotated every few years until Firoz Tughlaq.

q.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud, was written by:
q.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote it; Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir under Aibak.

q.s: Which of the following chronicle - author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Futuh-us-Salatin is by Isami; Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

q.s: The king 'Chandra' of the Mehrauli Iron Pillar is identified with:
q.x: The Iron Pillar is attributed to Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments' World Heritage Site?
q.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is at Tughlaqabad; the others are in the Qutb complex (WHS 1993).

q.s: Amir Khusrau's Tughluqnama deals with:
o: Meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad
q.x: Tughluqnama is on Ghiyasuddin's rise; Nuh Sipihr praises India under Mubarak Shah.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Amir Khusrau?
q.x: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi was written by Barani.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, called Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belonged to which Sufi order?
q.x: Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi and criticised Akbar's religious ideas from an orthodox standpoint.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT criticise Akbar's religious ideas from an orthodox standpoint?
q.x: Abul Fazl was Akbar's admirer and chronicler.

q.s: The du-aspa sih-aspa rank in the mansabdari system was introduced by:
q.x: Jahangir introduced it, first for Mahabat Khan; Akbar introduced the mansabdari system itself.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT introduced by Akbar?
q.x: Du-aspa sih-aspa came under Jahangir.

q.s: Who among the following built the Lohagarh fort at Bharatpur?
q.x: Suraj Mal, called the 'Plato of the Jat tribe', built Lohagarh.

q.s: The Jantar Mantar observatories at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura were built by:
q.x: Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber built all five observatories.

q.s: Which Mughal painter was sent by Jahangir to Persia to paint Shah Abbas and his court?
q.x: Bishan Das went with Jahangir's embassy to Persia.

q.s: Which of the following painters did NOT belong to Akbar's atelier?
q.x: Mansur, the animal painter, belonged to Jahangir's court.

q.s: Among the disciples of Ramananda, Raidas was by profession a:
q.x: Raidas was a cobbler; Kabir was a weaver, Sena a barber and Dhanna a Jat.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a disciple of Ramananda?
q.x: Kabir, Raidas, Pipa, Sena and Dhanna were Ramananda's disciples; Guru Nanak was not.

q.s: The Tallapaka family of composers is associated with which shrine?
q.x: Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family sang at Tirumala.

q.s: Which of the following saint-poet - place pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kshetrayya is associated with Muvva.

q.s: In which year did Shivaji die?
q.x: Shivaji died in 1680; 1689 is the year Sambhaji was executed and 1674 that of his coronation.

q.s: Madanna and Akkanna were ministers of which kingdom?
q.x: They served Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda and arranged his 1677 alliance with Shivaji.

q.s: Which of the following European trading companies was formed earliest?
q.x: English 1600, Dutch 1602, Danish 1616, French 1664.

q.s: Which of the following company - year of formation pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The French company was formed in 1664 under Colbert.

q.s: Tranquebar on the Coromandel coast was a settlement of the:
q.x: Tranquebar was Danish; Serampore was their Bengal base.

q.s: Which of the following settlement - European power pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Chandernagore was French.

q.s: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow?
q.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow; Nana Sahib at Kanpur and Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur.

q.s: Which of the following centre - leader pairs of the Revolt of 1857 is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: At Delhi the revolt was led in the name of Bahadur Shah II, with Bakht Khan as military leader.

q.s: Who was the real military leader of the rebels at Delhi in 1857?
q.x: General Bakht Khan, who came from Bareilly, led the rebel forces at Delhi.

q.s: Khan Bahadur Khan led the Revolt of 1857 at:
q.x: Khan Bahadur Khan proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam at Bareilly in Rohilkhand.

q.s: The name 'Rayalaseema' was proposed in 1928 by:
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed it; the Nandyal Andhra Mahasabha approved it.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the districts ceded by the Nizam in 1800?
q.x: On 12 October 1800 the Nizam ceded Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary in lieu of the subsidy.

q.s: The 'Sunset Law' is associated with which land revenue system?
q.x: Under the Permanent Settlement an estate was sold if revenue was unpaid by sunset of the due date.

q.s: Which Act gave occupancy rights to tenants in Bengal and Bihar?
q.x: The Bengal Tenancy Act 1885; the Haftam and Panjam Regulations instead strengthened zamindars.

q.s: The Montagu Declaration promising progressive realisation of responsible government was made in:
q.x: It was made on 20 August 1917; the Montagu-Chelmsford Report followed in 1918.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Montagu Declaration is correct?
o: It was made in response to pressure from the Swaraj Party.
It promised immediate Dominion Status to India.
It was issued after the Government of India Act 1919.
Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy when it was made.
q.x: Chelmsford was Viceroy and Montagu Secretary of State; the pressure came from the Home Rule movement (the Swaraj Party arose only in 1923).

q.s: Which Brahmo leader of Andhra joined the Justice Party, leading to splits in the movement?
q.x: Splits after Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Justice Party contributed to the Brahmo decline in Andhra.

q.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed under which Governor-General?
q.x: It was passed under Canning in 1856; Dalhousie had left earlier that year.

q.s: Under whose leadership was the first widow remarriage held in Bengal in December 1856?
q.x: Vidyasagar organised the first remarriage on 7 December 1856.

q.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 at:
q.x: Blavatsky and Olcott founded it at New York in 1875; it came to India in 1879.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Theosophical Society is correct?
o: It came to India in 1879 and is called Divya Gnana Samajam in Telugu.
It was founded by Annie Besant.
q.x: Blavatsky and Olcott founded it at New York in 1875; Annie Besant joined later.

q.s: Rast Goftar, the organ of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, was edited by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji edited Rast Goftar; the Sabha worked for girls' education and Parsi marriage reform.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha is correct?
o: It was a Sikh reform society.
It was founded by Jyotiba Phule.
Its organ Rast Goftar was edited by Behramji Malabari.
It worked for girls' education and reform of Parsi marriage customs.
q.x: It was a Parsi reform body; Dadabhai Naoroji edited Rast Goftar.

q.s: The Butler Committee (1927) was appointed to examine:
o: Reform of the Indian Civil Service
Relations between princely states and the Paramount Power
q.x: Chaired by Harcourt Butler, it examined relations between the princely states and the Paramount Power.

q.s: The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at which Congress session?
q.x: At Lahore in 1929, after the one-year deadline set at Calcutta in 1928 lapsed.

q.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Congress (1929)?
q.x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided; Motilal Nehru presided at Calcutta in 1928.

q.s: Who led the defence of the INA officers in the Red Fort trials?
q.x: Bhulabhai Desai led the INA Defence Committee's counsel.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the INA defence team at the Red Fort?
q.x: Nehru, Asaf Ali, Katju, Sapru and Sarat Bose were in the defence; Patel was not.

q.s: Who led the Chirala-Perala movement against the formation of a municipality?
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the residents' exodus from Chirala to Ramnagar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Chirala-Perala movement is correct?
o: It was a forest satyagraha in the Rampa region.
It was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
It was a protest against the formation of a municipality and its taxes.
q.x: Residents led by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya left the town in protest.

q.s: The JVP Committee on linguistic states consisted of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and:
q.x: Its 1949 report first rejected linguistic states, putting unity and security first.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the JVP Committee is correct?
o: Its report of April 1949 at first rejected the creation of linguistic States.
It was headed by Fazl Ali.
It was appointed after the formation of Andhra State.
It recommended the immediate creation of Andhra State.
q.x: It put unity, security and economic prosperity first after Partition.

q.s: Who is called the 'Iron Man of India' for integrating the princely states?
q.x: Patel integrated over 560 princely states into the Union, with V.P. Menon as his secretary.

q.s: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by:
q.x: The women of Bardoli gave Patel the title 'Sardar' after this no-tax campaign.

q.s: On Justice Mishra's report, Bellary taluk was given to:
q.x: Bellary taluk went to Mysore, while Rayadurg, Adoni and Alur went to Andhra.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the common High Court of the two states was located at:
q.x: Section 30 of the Act provided for a common High Court at Hyderabad.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is correct?
o: The common High Court sat at Amaravati.
Employees of State PSUs continue in their posts for three years under Section 82.
Arrears of taxes other than property tax are divided by population.
An order removing difficulties under Section 108 could be made only within two years of the appointed day.
q.x: PSU employees continue for one year; such arrears go by place of assessment; the common High Court was at Hyderabad.

q.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when President's Rule ended in December 1973?
q.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao took office after the State's first President's Rule (January-December 1973).

q.s: The Jai Andhra agitation was called off in October 1973 after the announcement of the:
q.x: It ended after the Six-Point Formula; the 32nd Amendment followed in December 1973.

q.s: Who among the following was a leader of the Jai Andhra movement of 1972-73?
q.x: Kakani Venkataratnam, B.V. Subba Reddy and Tenneti Viswanatham led Jai Andhra; the others are linked with the Telangana movements.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Jai Andhra movement is correct?
o: Its main grievance was that Andhras were treated as 'outsiders' in Hyderabad.
It demanded the merger of Andhra with Tamil Nadu.
It was led by Konda Laxman Bapuji.
q.x: Students formed its core in 1972-73.

q.s: The K.C. Sivaramakrishnan Committee (2014) was set up to:
o: Recommend new districts for Andhra Pradesh
Divide the assets of the composite State
Suggest options for the new capital of Andhra Pradesh
q.x: The expert committee on the AP capital reported in August 2014 and opposed a single 'super capital'.

q.s: Which was the first North-Eastern State to be carved out of Assam with full statehood?
q.x: Nagaland became a State in 1963.

q.s: Which of the following became a State in 1987?
q.x: Goa, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh became States in 1987; Sikkim in 1975, Meghalaya in 1972 and Nagaland in 1963.

q.s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the first Telugu inscription, was issued by:
q.x: Dhananjaya Varma issued the Kalamalla (Kadapa) inscription; the Pedavegi plates are of the Salankayana Nandivarma II.

q.s: Which of the following statements about early Andhra inscriptions is correct?
o: The Kondamudi inscription was issued by Devavarma.
The Pedavegi plates of Nandivarma II give the first mention of Vishnu temples in Andhra.
The Eluru inscription was issued by Jayavarma.
The Kalamalla inscription is written only in Sanskrit.
q.x: Kalamalla is the first Telugu inscription; Kondamudi is Jayavarma's and Eluru Devavarma's.

q.s: Bavari, who sent sixteen disciples to the Buddha, had settled on the banks of the:
q.x: The Suttanipata says Bavari of Kosala settled on the Godavari in the Assaka region.

q.s: The capital of the Mulaka janapada, neighbour of Assaka, was:
q.x: Mulaka had its capital at Pratishthana (Paithan); Potana was Assaka's capital.

q.s: Many relics of the Amaravati stupa are today in the British Museum, London and the Government Museum at:
q.x: Amaravati sculptures were taken to London and Madras (Chennai) museums.

q.s: International Museum Day is observed every year on:
q.x: 18 May is International Museum Day; 18 April is World Heritage Day.

q.s: Which ruler assumed the title 'Dakshinapatheshwara' (Lord of the Deccan)?
q.x: Pulakesin II; Harsha was called Sakalottarapathanatha.

q.s: Which of the following ruler-title pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Samudragupta was Kaviraja; Dakshinapatheshwara was Pulakesin II's title.

q.s: The Pallava king who destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title 'Vatapikonda' was:
q.x: Narasimhavarman I defeated and killed Pulakesin II.

q.s: The first capital of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi was:
q.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana ruled from Pishtapura (Pithapuram); Rajahmundry became capital much later.

q.s: Vikramankadevacharita, a biography of Vikramaditya VI, was written by:
q.x: Bilhana, court poet of the Kalyani Chalukya Vikramaditya VI, wrote it.

q.s: In Kakatiya villages, the twelve village servants were known as:
q.x: The Ayagars were paid by a share of produce and rent-free land.

q.s: In the Kakatiya village administration, the Karanam was the:
q.x: The Karanam kept accounts; the Talari was the watchman.

q.s: Which scholar described the Kakatiya age as the 'Golden Age of the Shudras'?
q.x: Talbot used the phrase; Burton Stein proposed the 'segmentary state' model.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the successor states that arose in Andhra after the fall of the Kakatiyas in 1323?
q.x: The Reddis, Musunuris and Recherla Velamas emerged after 1323; the Eastern Gangas were an older Kalinga dynasty.

q.s: The founder of the Reddi kingdom, who expelled the Tughlaq forces and ruled from Addanki, was:
q.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi founded the kingdom with Addanki as capital.

q.s: Which Reddi ruler abolished the tax on gold and developed the port of Motupalli?
q.x: Anavota Reddi developed Motupalli; Racha Vema was the last Kondavidu king.

q.s: Who succeeded Anavema Reddi on the Kondavidu throne?
q.x: Kumaragiri succeeded Anavema; his brother-in-law Kataya Vema later held Rajahmundry and reached Cuttack.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Kondavidu Reddis is correct?
o: Kumaragiri Reddi succeeded Prolaya Vema Reddi.
Kataya Vema, Kumaragiri's brother-in-law, conquered the east up to Cuttack.
q.x: Kumaragiri succeeded Anavema; Pedakomati opposed him and was made feudatory of Chandolu.

q.s: Akbar annexed Bengal in the year:
q.x: Bengal was annexed in 1576; Gujarat in 1572-73.

q.s: Jaunpur was conquered from the Sharqis by:
q.x: Bahlul Lodi took Jaunpur around 1479.

q.s: Who presented the Kohinoor diamond to Shah Jahan?
q.x: Mir Jumla, the Golconda noble who joined the Mughals, presented it; Tavernier only recorded it.

q.s: The Kohinoor diamond is believed to have come from which mine of the Golconda kingdom?
q.x: Kollur on the Krishna (Guntur district) was the famous Golconda diamond mine.

q.s: The Qutb Shahi kingdom of Golconda was annexed by Aurangzeb in:
q.x: Golconda fell in 1687, a year after Bijapur (1686).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the five Deccan Sultanates?
q.x: The Sharqis ruled Jaunpur in north India.

q.s: Which foreign visitor gave an eyewitness description of Krishnadevaraya's appearance and the 'House of Victory'?
q.x: Domingo Paes described the king and the Mahanavami Dibba.

q.s: Which of the following foreign writers did NOT visit Vijayanagara?
q.x: Babur only mentioned the king in his memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.

q.s: The Recherla Velamas ruled from:
q.x: The Recherla Velamas held Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

q.s: Which of the following Velama family - estate pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Ravus held Bobbili; Venkatagiri was the Velugotis'.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Vijayanagara temple architecture?
o: Pillared corridors added to older temples
q.x: Vijayanagara temples are Dravidian in style; the curvilinear shikhara is a Nagara feature.

q.s: The ruins of Vijayanagara, the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, are at:
q.x: Hampi on the Tungabhadra is a World Heritage Site.

q.s: In 1953, which town was chosen as the capital of Andhra State?
q.x: Kurnool became the capital, though the PSP wanted Tirupati.

q.s: The Praja Socialist Party (1952) was formed by merging the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party with the:
q.x: The KMPP and the Socialist Party merged to form the PSP in September 1952.

q.s: In 1911, a series of articles in The Hindu on the backward position of the Telugu people was written by:
q.x: Gurunatham of Guntur wrote six articles in April 1911, giving the low share of Andhras in services.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Jonnavittula Gurunatham's articles of 1911 is correct?
o: They demanded merger with Hyderabad State.
They showed that Andhras held far fewer posts in the services than non-Andhras.
q.x: In The Hindu he put the civil services at 56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras.

q.s: Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao in the year:
q.x: It began as a weekly in 1908; he also started the literary monthly Bharati in 1924.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is correct?
o: He founded Krishna Patrika at Machilipatnam.
He founded Andhra Patrika and the monthly Bharati.
q.x: Andhra Patrika 1908, Bharati 1924; Krishna Patrika was founded by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao.

q.s: Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 at:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao founded it at Machilipatnam.

q.s: Who edited Krishna Patrika from 1907 until his death in 1945?
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it for nearly four decades.

q.s: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu is associated with which art form?
q.x: He is the father of Telugu Harikatha, a solo narrative form.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a folk art form of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Bihu is a dance of Assam.

q.s: The Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS) was founded in 1994 by:
q.x: Manda Krishna Madiga founded the MRPS on 7 July 1994; he received the Padma Shri in 2025.

q.s: The MRPS was founded at Eedumudi village in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Eedumudi is in Prakasam district.

q.s: The Nandi Awards for films, television and drama are given by the:
q.x: They are a State honour instituted by Andhra Pradesh in 1964; the National Film Awards are presented by the President.

Reservation of seats for STs in Lok Sabha

Free APSRTC bus travel for women

Jagananna colony houses under Pedalandariki Illu were launched on 3 June 2021.

Removal of an elected representative before the end of his term

q.x: Article 24; Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour.

Claims of SCs and STs to services

Article 335 - Claims of SCs and STs to services
Article 351 - Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 350A - Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage

o: It can be introduced in either House.
It can be referred to a joint sitting.

Restored the term of the Lok Sabha to five years

The Speaker vacates office as soon as the Lok Sabha is dissolved.

q.s: As per PLFS 2023-24, India's female Labour Force Participation Rate (15+, usual status) was:

q.s: Which of the following statements about female LFPR in India (PLFS) is correct?
o: Urban female LFPR is higher than rural female LFPR.
Female LFPR is above 60% at present.
Female LFPR has fallen in every round since 2020-21.
Rural female LFPR is higher than urban female LFPR.
q.x: In 2025 rural female LFPR was about 45.9% and urban about 27.7%.

q.s: The concept of the 'vicious circle of poverty' is associated with:
q.x: Nurkse: low income - low saving - low investment - low productivity - low income.

q.s: As per NITI Aayog, India's national multidimensional poverty headcount fell from 55.3% in 2005-06 to what in 2019-21?
q.x: It fell to 14.96% in 2019-21 (NFHS-5).

q.s: Which of the following statements about poverty in India is correct?
o: The national MPI is prepared by the RBI.
The MDG base year for halving poverty was 2000.
India's national MPI headcount rose between 2005-06 and 2019-21.
India met the MDG target of halving extreme poverty.
q.x: The MDG base year was 1990; NITI Aayog's MPI fell from 55.3% to 14.96%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about NITI Aayog is correct?
o: It has no power to allocate plan funds to the States.
It prepares Five Year Plans for the States.
It was set up by an Act of Parliament.
q.x: NITI Aayog, set up by a Cabinet Resolution in 2015, is a think tank promoting cooperative and competitive federalism.

q.s: Who admitted in 1958 that the Planning Commission had become a kind of 'super-cabinet'?
q.x: Nehru himself made the admission.

q.s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula for central plan assistance, population carried a weight of:
q.x: Population 60%, per capita income 25%, fiscal performance 7.5%.

q.s: Under Gadgil-Mukherjee, Special Category States received central plan assistance in the grant : loan ratio of:
q.x: Special Category States got 90 : 10; General Category States like AP 30 : 70.

q.s: India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business index improved from 142 in 2014 to which rank in 2019?
q.x: India reached 63rd place in 2019.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh has held the top rank in the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) since:
q.x: AP has been No. 1 since BRAP 2016.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT shared with the States as part of the divisible pool of Central taxes?
q.x: Cesses and surcharges stay with the Union, aggravating the vertical fiscal imbalance.

q.s: The Finance Commission of India is constituted under Article:
q.x: It is constituted afresh by the President every five years or earlier; it is not a permanent body.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission is correct?
o: It is constituted by the President every five years or earlier.
It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
q.x: It is set up afresh under Article 280; it is not permanent.

q.s: Which of the following was among Andhra Pradesh's original three aspirational districts?
q.x: The original three were Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa.

q.s: After the 2022 reorganisation of districts, Vizianagaram was replaced in the Aspirational Districts Programme by:
q.x: Parvathipuram Manyam was carved out of Vizianagaram; YSR Kadapa continues.

q.s: Sustainable Development Goal 14 relates to:
q.x: SDG 14 is Life Below Water; Life on Land is SDG 15.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals?
q.x: UBI is not an SDG; SDG 2 is Zero Hunger, SDG 4 Quality Education and SDG 5 Gender Equality.

q.s: By what majority did the Supreme Court uphold the 2016 demonetisation in 2023?
q.x: A five-judge Bench upheld it 4 : 1.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rs 2,000 notes withdrawn in May 2023 is correct?
o: They were withdrawn under a new demonetisation law.
They ceased to be legal tender on withdrawal.
They continue to be legal tender.
q.x: The RBI withdrew them from circulation, but they remain legal tender.

q.s: Flexible inflation targeting was adopted by the RBI on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended it; the framework began in 2016.

q.s: Monetary targeting with feedback (M3-based) from 1985 was based on the report of the:
q.x: Sukhamoy Chakravarty Committee (1985).

q.s: The umbrella organisation for Urban Cooperative Banks is:
q.x: The National Urban Co-operative Finance and Development Corporation is the UCB umbrella body.

q.s: 'Sahakar Sarathi', the shared-services entity for cooperative banks, was set up by:
q.x: It is NABARD's entity, approved by the RBI.

q.s: In Lalit Kumar Jain (2021), the Supreme Court held that on approval of a resolution plan under the IBC, personal guarantors:
q.x: Approval of the plan does not release personal guarantors.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code is correct?
o: Under the IBC waterfall, workmen's dues rank above government dues.
Personal guarantors are released when a resolution plan is approved.
Government dues rank first in the IBC waterfall.
q.x: The IBC came in 2016; Lalit Kumar Jain (2021) kept guarantors liable.

q.s: The term 'twin deficits' refers to the:
o: Fiscal deficit and current account deficit
q.x: A higher fiscal deficit reduces national saving and widens the CAD.

q.s: Which Article provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law?
q.x: Article 265.

q.s: Which of the following statements about taxing powers under the Constitution is correct?
o: The State List has more taxing entries than the Union List.
The Union List has 20 taxing entries.
The residuary power of taxation lies with the States.
Article 266 says no tax shall be levied except by law.
q.x: The Union List has 15 and the State List 20 taxing entries; residuary power lies with Parliament; the rule is Article 265.

q.s: The Cost Inflation Index used for indexation of capital gains has the base year:
q.x: The CBDT's CII uses 2001-02 as base year.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a capital asset under the Income-tax Act?
q.x: Rural agricultural land is excluded from capital assets.

q.s: GST avoids the cascading effect ('tax on tax') mainly through:
q.x: Input tax credit removes tax on tax, making GST less inflationary.

q.s: Which of the following taxes was NOT subsumed in GST?
q.x: Basic customs duty continues; IGST applies on imports in addition.

q.s: The condition under which devaluation of a currency improves the trade balance is known as the:
q.x: Devaluation helps only if export and import demand elasticities together exceed one.

q.s: Which of the following statements about devaluation is correct?
o: By the J-curve, the trade balance improves first and worsens later.
It makes exports cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home.
It always improves the trade balance at once.
It makes imports cheaper at home.
q.x: By the J-curve the balance first worsens; it improves only if the Marshall-Lerner condition holds.

q.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India ran a surplus in FY25 in its:
q.x: India had a merchandise trade deficit of about $283.5 bn in FY25; the surplus was in services.

q.s: India recorded its first current account surplus in 24 years in:
q.x: The surplus of 2001-02 was the first in 24 years.

q.s: India's current account deficit peaked at about 4.8% of GDP in:
q.x: The CAD of FY13 was higher than the 1990-91 crisis level of about 3%.

q.s: India accepted the obligations of Article VIII of the IMF, making the rupee convertible on current account, in:
q.x: The rupee is fully convertible only on current account, since August 1994.

q.s: Which of the following statements about rupee convertibility is correct?
o: FEMA made foreign-exchange violations criminal offences.
India accepted IMF Article VIII in 1991.
The rupee is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts.
The rupee is fully convertible on current account but not fully on capital account.
q.x: Article VIII was accepted in August 1994; FEMA made violations civil offences.

q.s: India's present exchange-rate system is best described as a:
q.x: The rate is market-determined, with RBI intervention only to curb volatility.

q.s: Which of the following statements about exchange-rate regimes is correct?
o: India follows a fixed peg to the US dollar.
Under a fixed peg, the central bank never buys or sells foreign currency.
Under a managed float, the central bank intervenes only to curb volatility.
Under a managed float, the central bank alone fixes the rate.
q.x: India's rate is market-determined with RBI intervention against volatility.

q.s: The Planning Commission (1989) divided India into how many agro-climatic regions?
q.x: 15 regions and 72 sub-zones; 127 is the number of NARP agro-climatic zones.

q.s: The Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh falls in which agro-climatic region?
q.x: Rayalaseema is in the Southern Plateau and Hills; coastal AP is in the East Coast Plains and Hills.

q.s: The Yellow Revolution in India relates to the production of:
q.x: It began with the Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986) and continues through NMEO.

q.s: The Yellow Revolution is associated with:
q.x: Sam Pitroda headed the Technology Missions; Kurien is linked with the White Revolution.

q.s: In which Five Year Plan was agricultural growth the lowest (about 0.73%) because of droughts?
q.x: The Third Plan (1961-66) saw wars and droughts.

q.s: In which Five Year Plan did agriculture and allied sectors record the highest growth (about 4.68%)?
q.x: The Eighth Plan exceeded its 4.1% target.

q.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, support that requires farmers to limit production is placed in the:
q.x: Blue Box; Green Box support is allowed without limit.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Agriculture is correct?
o: Blue Box support covers export subsidies.
Green Box support is allowed without limit.
Green Box support is capped at the de minimis level.
The Amber Box de minimis limit is 5% for developing countries.
q.x: Green Box support is non-trade-distorting; the Amber Box de minimis is 10% for developing countries.

q.s: As per the NSSO 77th round, which State had the highest share of indebted agricultural households?
q.x: 93.2% of AP agricultural households were indebted, the highest in India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about rural distress in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Less than half of AP's agricultural households are indebted.
AP farmers depend only on institutional credit.
Gulf migration comes mainly from Anantapur.
Rayalaseema and Srikakulam are the main distress-migration belts.
q.x: 93.2% of households are indebted and about half of farmers use non-institutional credit; Gulf migration is mainly from Kadapa and Konaseema.

q.s: Which of the following is a pulse crop?
q.x: Gram is a pulse; groundnut is an oilseed and paddy a cereal.

q.s: Minimum Support Prices are recommended by the:
o: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
q.x: The CACP recommends MSPs; the Cabinet announces them.

q.s: The phase of industrial deceleration in India, with growth of about 4%, was:
q.x: Wars, droughts, infrastructure bottlenecks and licensing slowed industry in 1965-80.

q.s: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 aimed to raise manufacturing's share of GDP to:
q.x: The 25% target was missed; manufacturing is still about 16-17% of GVA.

q.s: The Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee that led to the IBC was headed by:
q.x: T.K. Viswanathan headed the BLRC.

q.s: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) was set up under the:
q.x: NCLT was set up under Section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013; BIFR was dissolved on 1 December 2016.

q.s: Which country topped the Global Gender Gap Index 2025?
q.x: Iceland was first; India was 131st of 148.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a sub-index of the Global Gender Gap Index?
q.x: The four sub-indices are economic participation, education, health and survival, and political empowerment.

q.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in the production of:
q.x: AP is 1st in eggs, 2nd in raw silk, 4th in meat and 7th in milk.

q.s: In which of the following does Andhra Pradesh NOT rank first in India (SES 2025-26)?
q.x: AP is 1st in eggs, fish and fruits but 7th in milk.

q.s: A rise in the Gini coefficient of State per capita incomes over time indicates:
q.x: The Gini of State PCI rose from 0.230 (1994-95) to 0.261 (2025-26), showing divergence.

q.s: Integrated GST (IGST) on inter-State supplies is provided under Article:
q.x: 269A - IGST; 246A - power to make GST laws; 279A - GST Council.

q.s: A 'vote on account' is provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 116; Article 110 defines a Money Bill and 114 deals with Appropriation Bills.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 is correct?
o: It shows a revenue deficit of about 1.1% of GSDP.
Its fiscal deficit is within the 3% norm.
Its capital outlay is lower than in the previous year.
q.x: Revenue deficit Rs 22,003 crore; fiscal deficit 3.8% of GSDP; capital outlay up about 47%.

q.s: Under Section 54 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the public debt of the undivided State was apportioned on the basis of:
q.x: Debt went by population ratio, except loans for projects confined to one State.

q.s: The Polavaram Project is being built across which river?
q.x: Polavaram is a national project on the Godavari.

q.s: The Centre funds 100% of the remaining cost of which component of the Polavaram Project?
q.x: Only the irrigation component, from 1 April 2014, to the extent of the cost on that date.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), launched in 2020, has an outlay of:
q.x: PMMSY - Rs 20,050 crore; PM-MKSSY - Rs 6,000 crore; FIDF - Rs 7,522 crore.

q.s: Which crop occupies the largest share of the food-grain area in Andhra Pradesh (2024-25)?
q.x: Paddy covered about 56% (20.97 of 37.51 lakh ha).

q.s: Which of the following statements about paddy in Andhra Pradesh (2024-25) is correct?
o: Maize covered the largest food-grain area.
Rabi paddy output was higher than kharif output.
Kharif paddy output was higher than rabi paddy output.
q.x: Kharif 78.79 lakh t against rabi 48.36 lakh t; food-grain area rose to 37.51 lakh ha.

q.s: The 'Sweet Revolution' relates to:
q.x: Sweet Revolution - honey; Yellow - oilseeds; Blue - fish.

q.s: Which of the following revolution - product pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Blue Revolution relates to fish.

q.s: Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh is known for the cultivation of:
q.x: Araku is famous for tribal-grown coffee.

q.s: Banganapalli, a GI-tagged product of Andhra Pradesh, is a variety of:
q.x: Banganapalli is a mango variety.

q.s: Before becoming an SEZ, the Visakhapatnam zone was a(n):
q.x: Visakhapatnam EPZ was converted into an SEZ.

q.s: The APSEZ at Atchutapuram, the largest SEZ of Andhra Pradesh, is located near:
q.x: Atchutapuram is near Visakhapatnam (Anakapalli area).

q.s: Which State has the largest number of operational SEZs in India at present?
q.x: Tamil Nadu leads in operational SEZs; Telangana has the most approved ones.

q.s: Nandigram, the site of the 2007 anti-SEZ protests, is in which district of West Bengal?
q.x: Nandigram is in Purba Medinipur; Singur (Tata Nano) is in Hooghly.

q.s: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Start-ups (2022) gives guarantees through the:
q.x: The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company runs it; it replaced the Credit Guarantee Fund for Startups.

q.s: Under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Start-ups, the guarantee cover per borrower is up to:
q.x: The October 2022 scheme covers up to Rs 20 crore per borrower.

q.s: Ratlam Municipality v. Vardhichand (1980) is associated with:
o: The duty of a municipality to remove public nuisance
q.x: Ratlam laid down the municipal duty on sanitation; absolute liability came from the Oleum gas case.

q.s: The Bichhri case (Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action, 1996) applied the:
q.x: It made the Rajasthan chemical units pay for the damage they caused.

q.s: Which planets are called the 'ice giants'?
q.x: Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants; Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an inner (terrestrial) planet?
q.x: Jupiter is a gas giant beyond the asteroid belt.

q.s: Spring tides occur when:
o: The Sun, Earth and Moon are in a straight line
The Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth
q.x: Spring tides come at new and full moon.

q.s: Neap tides occur during the:
o: First and third quarters of the Moon
q.x: At the quarters, the Sun and Moon pull at right angles, giving lower high tides.

q.s: The International Date Line passes through the:
q.x: It runs through the Bering Strait and zigzags to avoid land.

q.s: A traveller crossing the International Date Line eastward, from Asia to America, will:
o: Move the calendar forward by one day
Change the clock by one hour
Make no change in the date
Set the calendar back by one day
q.x: Going east the traveller repeats a day; going west a day is skipped.

q.s: India's first seismological observatory was set up in 1898 at:
q.x: The first observatory was at Alipore.

q.s: The earthquake-alert apps 'IndiaQuake' and 'RISEQ' are of the:
q.x: Both are NCS/MoES apps.

q.s: Manikaran hot spring is in which State?
q.x: Manikaran is in the Parvati valley of Kullu.

q.s: Which of the following hot spring - State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Tattapani is in Chhattisgarh.

q.s: A flat-topped seamount, planed by waves and later submerged, is called a:
q.x: A guyot; a seamount is a volcanic peak that does not reach the surface.

q.s: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a central lagoon is called a(n):
q.x: Lakshadweep has many atolls.

q.s: The Gobi desert lies in:
q.x: The Gobi lies in Mongolia and northern China.

q.s: Which of the following deserts is NOT in the Southern Hemisphere?
q.x: The Gobi is in Mongolia and northern China.

q.s: The Great Dividing Range lies in:
q.x: The Great Dividing Range (about 3,500 km) is longer than the Himalayas.

q.s: Which of the following mountain ranges is NOT in the Americas?
q.x: The Great Dividing Range is in Australia.

q.s: The shrinking of the Dead Sea is mainly due to the diversion of the waters of the river:
q.x: Diversion of the Jordan and mineral extraction are draining it.

q.s: The highest temperatures on the Earth are recorded over the:
q.x: Clear skies and dry air let maximum insolation reach the subtropical deserts.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the distribution of temperature is correct?
o: Cloud cover increases insolation at the Equator.
The highest temperatures are recorded over subtropical deserts.
Polar regions receive the most insolation in a year.
The highest temperatures are recorded at the Equator.
q.x: Clear skies and dry air let maximum insolation reach the subtropical deserts.

q.s: Which cloud forms a thin milky sheet that produces a halo round the Sun or Moon?
q.x: Cirrostratus produces the halo.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a high cloud?
q.x: Altostratus is a middle cloud.

q.s: Which of the following statements about cyclones is correct?
o: Tropical cyclones are smaller and more intense than temperate cyclones.
Temperate cyclones cover a smaller area than tropical cyclones.
Temperate cyclones generally move from east to west.
Temperate cyclones occur mainly between 5° and 30° latitudes.
q.x: Temperate cyclones occur at 35°-65°, cover larger areas with gentler winds and move west to east.

q.s: Temperate cyclones generally move:
q.x: They move with the westerlies.

q.s: Thermohaline circulation in the oceans is driven mainly by differences in:
q.x: Cold, saline polar water sinks and creeps towards the equator.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a warm ocean current?
q.x: The Labrador Current is cold.

q.s: Oceans absorb what share of the excess heat caused by global warming?
q.x: Oceans take up over 90% of the excess heat.

q.s: The highest surface temperatures of ocean water are found:
q.x: The thermal equator lies just north of the equator.

q.s: Which of the following is a freshwater lake?
q.x: Utah Lake is fresh; the others are highly saline.

q.s: Lake Van, a closed soda lake with very high salinity, is in:
q.x: Lake Van in eastern Turkey has a salinity of about 330 per thousand.

q.s: The main source of the salts in the oceans is:
q.x: Most ocean salts come from rivers; higher salinity lowers evaporation.

q.s: An isohaline is a line joining places of equal:
q.x: Isohalines show equal salinity; isotherms show equal temperature.

q.s: Kodaikanal hill station lies in which hills?
q.x: Kodaikanal is in the Palani hills; Yercaud is in the Shevaroy hills.

q.s: Which of the following hills - hill station pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Yercaud is in the Shevaroy hills.

q.s: When Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956, it had how many districts?
q.x: AP started with 20 districts; residual AP had 13 in 2014.

q.s: On 4 April 2022, the number of districts in Andhra Pradesh was raised from 13 to:
q.x: The State reorganised into 26 districts under its own districts law.

q.s: Ooty is much cooler than Coimbatore mainly because of its:
q.x: Temperature falls with height.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a factor controlling the climate of a place?
q.x: Latitude, altitude and distance from the sea are climatic controls.

q.s: Ralegan Siddhi village is known for overcoming its water crisis through:
o: Watershed development with check dams and tanks
q.x: Ralegan Siddhi became a model of watershed development.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a drought-prevention measure?
q.x: Eucalyptus draws heavily on groundwater.

q.s: The river Nagavali is also known as:
q.x: Nagavali - Langulya; Vedavathi - Hagari; Swarnamukhi - Mogaleru; Penna - Pinakini.

q.s: Which of the following river - other name pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Swarnamukhi is also called Mogaleru.

q.s: The MISHTI programme, launched on 5 June 2023, relates to:
q.x: MISHTI is Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes.

q.s: As per ISFR, which State has the largest mangrove cover in India?
q.x: West Bengal (Sundarbans) leads; AP is behind West Bengal, Gujarat and A&N.

q.s: In the India State of Forest Report, 'scrub' is degraded forest land with canopy density below:
q.x: Scrub (canopy under 10%) is not counted as forest cover; AP's 38,436.58 sq km figure includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub.

q.s: Which animal was declared India's national aquatic animal in 2009?
q.x: The Gangetic river dolphin was declared the national aquatic animal in 2009.

q.s: Under PMMSY, the subsidy for women, SC and ST beneficiaries is:
q.x: 60% for women, SC and ST; 40% for general beneficiaries.

q.s: What is India's rank among the fish-producing countries of the world?
q.x: India is second after China; inland fisheries give more than 75% of output.

q.s: Which item leads India's seafood exports?
q.x: Frozen shrimp is the top seafood export.

q.s: A resource that is available but cannot be used for lack of technology, such as hydrogen from water, is called a:
q.x: Stock; the part of the stock usable with present technology is a reserve.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a biotic resource?
q.x: Minerals are abiotic.

q.s: Bauxite deposits are typically formed by:
q.x: Bauxite results from residual weathering (laterisation).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT typically found in placer deposits?
q.x: Coal occurs in sedimentary beds.

q.s: The Ravva oil field in the Krishna-Godavari basin has been operated since 1996 by:
q.x: Ravva was found by ONGC in 1987 and is operated by Cairn.

q.s: The deepwater KG-D6 gas block is operated by:
q.x: KG-D6 is Reliance's block with BP as partner.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh holds about what share of India's heavy-mineral beach sand resources?
q.x: AP has about 327 of India's 1,078 million tonnes, about 30.4%.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a heavy mineral found in beach sands?
q.x: Bauxite is a residual deposit; ilmenite, monazite and zircon occur in beach sands.

q.s: Which is the leading milk-producing district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Chittoor leads; AP ranked 7th in milk in 2023-24.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's livestock sector is correct?
o: Prakasam is AP's leading milk-producing district.
AP ranks first in India in meat production.
AP ranks first in India in milk production.
AP ranks first in India in egg production.
q.x: AP is 1st in eggs, 7th in milk and 4th in meat; Chittoor leads in milk.

q.s: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) was formed in the year:
q.x: HAL was formed in 1964 from Hindustan Aircraft (1940).

q.s: Hindustan Aircraft, the forerunner of HAL, was founded in 1940 at:
q.x: It was founded at Bengaluru by Walchand Hirachand.

q.s: Which country is the largest exporter of sugar in the world?
q.x: Brazil is the largest exporter; India the largest producer.

q.s: Which of the following world market - leading country pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Indonesia leads in palm oil, followed by Malaysia.

q.s: Rushikonda, Andhra Pradesh's Blue Flag beach, is in which district?
q.x: Rushikonda is in Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Which of the following beach - district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Baruva is in Srikakulam.

q.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
q.x: AP scored 74 and was 9th, in the Front Runner category.

q.s: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index of NITI Aayog uses how many indicators?
q.x: The national MPI has 3 dimensions and 12 indicators; the global MPI has 10.

q.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the lowest multidimensional poverty?
q.x: West Godavari; AP's headcount (6.06%) is well below India's (14.96%).

q.s: Which of the following is one of the new districts created in Andhra Pradesh in 2025?
q.x: Polavaram and Markapuram were created in 2025; the others date from 2022.

q.s: According to Census 2011, how many towns were there in India?
q.x: 7,935 towns: 4,041 statutory and 3,894 census towns.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the number of statutory towns in India was:
q.x: 4,041 statutory towns; census towns rose from 1,362 in 2001 to 3,894.

q.s: The gap between urban and rural population growth in India is mainly explained by:
q.x: Natural increase is similar in both, so migration explains the gap.

q.s: The Lepcha tribe is mainly found in:
q.x: The Lepchas live in Sikkim.

q.s: Which of the following tribe - State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Kharwar live in Uttar Pradesh (and Jharkhand), not Sikkim.

q.s: The Khasi language belongs to which language family?
q.x: Khasi is Austro-Asiatic (Mon-Khmer); Bodo is Sino-Tibetan.

q.s: Which of the following language - family pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic branch of Indo-Aryan.

q.s: Zooxanthellae, which give corals food and colour, are:
q.x: They are dinoflagellate algae living in coral tissues.

q.s: Coral skeletons are made of calcium carbonate in the form of:
